content:
The image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, scattered pustules/lesions across the leaf surface. Key observations:

- Small, oval to circular pustules scattered across both the upper and visible lower leaf surfaces
- The pustules appear reddish-brown/orange-tan in color
- They are distributed randomly across the leaf, not in bands along veins
- Lesions are small (under 1/4 inch), oval to elongate shaped
- The leaf itself is otherwise green and healthy looking
- No rectangular vein-bounded lesions (rules out Gray Leaf Spot)
- No large cigar-shaped lesions (rules out Northern Leaf Blight)
- Pustules appear on the upper leaf surface and are somewhat circular and densely packed, with a light orange to cinnamon color

The small, circular-to-oval orange pustules densely packed and appearing predominantly on the upper leaf surface match Southern Rust. Common Rust pustules tend to be more elongate, darker reddish-brown, and appear on both leaf surfaces equally. The pustules here look more circular, lighter orange, and dense on the upper surface — characteristic of Southern Rust.
